metaDescription: Six small trash can sets compared by capacity, footprint, handles, bag holders and lids, from an 8-pack of 3-gallon baskets to a slim lidded 3-pack.
introParagraphs: Small trash cans are bought in bundles, which is why picking the right set matters more than picking a single can. A pack of eight baskets can outfit an entire apartment, while a pack of three suits a bathroom, a bedroom and an office. Size, shape, handle and bag holder all affect how the baskets live in your home.

This lineup is built from sets rather than single cans. The Sterilite comes in a pack of eight 3-gallon rectangular baskets, the BGUP is a five-pack of 3.5-gallon cans with a roll of bags, and the JiatuA is a round three-pack measuring 7.9 inches across. The JOYMOOP and UUJOLY include four rolls of bags, and the NETDOT adds a lid to a slim 2.6-gallon design.

We evaluated each set on the listing specs and buyer feedback themes, thinking about where the cans will actually sit: beside a toilet, under a desk, next to a bed or inside a cabinet. A small can that does not fit its spot is worse than none.

products.name: BGUP 3.5 Gallon Small Trash Can 5-Pack with Bags
products.description:
The BGUP set offers the most capacity per can among the multipacks that include bags. Each basket holds 3.5 gallons, which is large enough for a bedroom, a home office or a small kitchen counter, and five of them cover most of a household. The listing includes one roll of garbage bags, so the baskets can go to work on the day they arrive.

The design is a modern, simple black plastic with a smooth, non-textured surface that the listing calls wear-resistant and scratch-resistant. Smooth sides make wiping easy, which matters for baskets that sit in bathrooms and kitchens. The footprint is given as 8.66 inches by 5.71 inches at the bottom, and the top opening is longer and wider, which makes tossing items in easier.

Because the top opens wide, there is no lid, so the contents show and odors are not contained. That is the usual tradeoff of small open baskets. Compared with the Sterilite eight-pack, you get fewer cans but more capacity per can. Compared with the NETDOT, you give up the lid. For a household that wants a generous number of mid-size baskets with bags included, this is the best all-round set.
products.bestFor: Households that want five roomy baskets plus a starter roll of bags.
pros: Five baskets cover most of a home
Roll of bags included in the set
cons: Open top shows contents and odors
Wide opening takes more shelf space

products.name: Sterilite 3 Gallon Rectangular Wastebasket 8-Pack
products.description:
When a project calls for lots of baskets, the Sterilite eight-pack stands out. Each rectangular wastebasket holds 3 gallons and has an open top, so one set can equip bedrooms, bathrooms, offices and a rental property without a second order. The sleek lines suit most interiors.

The textured surface is a thoughtful touch. Unlike the smooth sides on the BGUP, texture hides scuff marks and residue, which keeps a basket looking tidy after months of use. The listing describes the material as built to withstand daily use, and says it is easy to clean.

Eight identical baskets are an advantage only if you need that many. Otherwise you have a pile of storage to find homes for. The 3-gallon size is slightly smaller than the BGUP, and no bags are listed in the pack. Compared with the JOYMOOP and UUJOLY sets, you lose included bags but gain a much higher count. If you manage several rooms or a small property, this pack makes the most sense.
products.bestFor: Landlords, large families and anyone outfitting many rooms.
cons: No bags listed in the pack
Too many for a single room

products.name: JiatuA 1.8 Gallon Round Trash Can 3-Pack with Bags
products.description:
The JiatuA is a set of three round baskets sized for narrow corners. Each measures 7.9 inches across and 9.8 inches tall, with a capacity of 1.8 gallons, or 6.8 liters. That small footprint fits beside a toilet, under a desk or between a nightstand and a wall, and the three-pack includes trash bags.

The material is described as new thickened PP plastic with good toughness. The listing says it does not deform when squeezed, which is helpful in a corner where a bin gets pushed. The lidless, large-opening design means you can drop items in without touching a lid, and a raised bottom adds a little stability.

A 1.8-gallon basket fills fast, so expect to empty it more often than the BGUP. Without a lid it does nothing for odor. Compared with the NETDOT, it is less discreet but easier to use with one hand. Compared with the UUJOLY set, the round shape wastes a bit more corner space but offers a firmer feel. For a bathroom or bedside use, it is a neat and affordable set.
products.bestFor: Narrow corners and bedside or bathroom use.
cons: Round shape wastes some wall space

products.name: JOYMOOP 2.2 Gallon Slim Trash Can 3-Pack with Bags
products.description:
The JOYMOOP set trades round for slim. The three baskets each hold 2.2 gallons, a middle size between the JiatuA and the BGUP, and a compact design suits placement next to a toilet or under a desk. The package includes four rolls of bags, which is generous for baskets this small.

The plastic is described as high quality, resisting chipping, denting and fading even with regular use. That matters in a bathroom, where steam and splashes can age cheap plastic. The listing positions the set for offices, bathrooms, bedrooms and kitchens, so it is flexible.

Bags are the quiet selling point. Small-basket liners can be hard to find, and four rolls will last a long time. The shape is simple and open, so there is no lid, no pedal and no extras. Compared with the BGUP, you get fewer cans and less volume, but more bags. Compared with the UUJOLY set, the listing shows no built-in handle or bag holder. For a household that wants slim baskets and plenty of liners, it is a sensible choice.
products.bestFor: Slim spaces where plenty of small liners matter.
cons: Open top offers no odor control
No handle or bag holder listed

products.badge: Best with Handle and Bag Holder
products.name: UUJOLY Small Trash Can 3-Pack with Handle and Bag Holder
products.description:
The UUJOLY set focuses on two practical details that most small baskets ignore. Each basket has a built-in handle for easy carrying and a dedicated bag holder slot that helps keep the liner secure. If you have ever fished a slipped bag out of a basket, you will appreciate the second feature.

The baskets are black durable plastic with a smooth surface that makes cleaning simple, and the listing says they fit neatly beside toilets, under sinks, next to desks or beside beds. Four rolls of bags come in the box, which gives you a starter supply.

The listing does not give a capacity figure in the text we have, so we cannot rank it on size. We can say it is a plain open basket without a lid, which limits odor control. Compared with the JOYMOOP, it adds the handle and bag holder. Compared with the BGUP, it offers fewer cans in the pack. If you carry baskets to a sink to empty them or you hate slipping bags, it is the most thoughtful design here.
products.bestFor: People who carry baskets to empty them and hate slipping bags.
pros: Bag holder slot keeps liners put
cons: Capacity not given in the listing text

products.name: N. NETDOT 2.6 Gallon Slim Trash Can with Lid 3-Pack
products.description:
The NETDOT is the only set in this group with a lid. Each can holds 10 liters, or 2.6 gallons, and the compact, sleek design suits tight spaces such as bathrooms. The listing says the lid provides a secure barrier to keep pets out of the trash, which is a real advantage over open baskets.

Smooth surfaces and clean lines make it easy to keep the cans tidy, and the listing says the cans help trap smells inside. A lid shields the contents from sight, which matters in a bathroom or bedroom where an open basket can look untidy. Three cans cover several rooms.

The lid adds a step each time you throw something away, and the listing in our data does not describe how it opens. Without bags included, you have to supply your own liners. Compared with the JOYMOOP, you gain a lid but lose included bags, and compared with the BGUP, you get a smaller capacity. If you have a curious pet or want to hide contents, it is the best fit here.
products.bestFor: Homes with pets or anyone who wants contents hidden.
pros: Lid keeps pets out of the trash
Slim sleek profile fits tight spots
cons: Lid adds a step to each use
No bags listed in the set

buyingCriteria.explanation: Small baskets range from about 1.8 gallons to 3.5 gallons in this lineup. The JiatuA holds 1.8 gallons, the JOYMOOP 2.2, the NETDOT 2.6, the Sterilite 3 and the BGUP 3.5. A larger basket empties less often but takes more space. Match size to how much waste the spot produces, such as a bedside versus a kitchen counter. A bedside basket may only collect tissues, so a 1.8-gallon size is plenty, while a desk that sees snack wrappers and paper will outgrow it within days. If in doubt, pick the larger size and empty it before it overflows.

Round baskets like the JiatuA suit corners, rectangular ones like the Sterilite sit flush to walls, and slim designs like the NETDOT slide into gaps. The JiatuA measures 7.9 inches across and the BGUP bottom is 8.66 by 5.71 inches. Measure the spot before choosing. A basket that sticks out becomes a shin hazard.

Open baskets are fast to use and simple, while a lid hides contents and traps odor. The NETDOT is the only lidded set here, and the listing says it keeps pets out. For bedrooms and bathrooms with guests, a lid is worth the extra step. For desks and workshops, open is usually fine.

Small liners can be hard to find, so a set with bags in the box saves effort. The JOYMOOP and UUJOLY each include four rolls, the BGUP includes one, and the JiatuA includes bags as well. The UUJOLY adds a dedicated bag holder slot, which stops slipping. Check the bag size recommended before buying more.

Small baskets are often carried to a larger bin, so a handle matters. The UUJOLY has a built-in handle, while others rely on grabbing the rim. A handle also helps you lift the basket for cleaning. If you empty baskets into a central bag, prefer a model with one.

Smooth surfaces wipe clean easily, as on the BGUP and UUJOLY, while textured surfaces such as the Sterilite hide scuffs. Both approaches work; pick based on whether you prefer tidy-looking baskets or faster wiping. Avoid baskets with deep seams where residue collects. A smooth basket like the BGUP is quickest to wipe after a spill, while the Sterilite texture forgives the scuffs that come from being shoved under a desk. Think about which annoyance you meet more often.

faq.q: What size is a small trash can?
faq.a: Small cans in this lineup range from 1.8 to 3.5 gallons. The JiatuA is 1.8 gallons and the BGUP is 3.5. Choose by how much waste the spot generates.

faq.q: Do small trash cans need bags?
faq.a: Bags keep the basket clean and make emptying easier. Several sets here include bags, such as the JOYMOOP and UUJOLY with four rolls each. Check the bag size before buying more. Since small liners come in several shapes, test one in a single basket before you stock up on a large supply.

faq.q: Is a lid necessary on a small can?
faq.a: It depends on the room. A lid hides contents and helps with odor, as on the NETDOT. In an office or workshop an open basket is usually enough.

faq.q: How many baskets should I buy?
faq.a: Count the rooms that need one, then add a spare. A five-pack like the BGUP covers most homes, while the Sterilite eight-pack suits larger needs. Avoid buying more than you can store. Extra baskets can also stand in for a recycling bin or a laundry-room sorter, which makes a larger pack useful beyond trash. If you are unsure, start with a pack of three and add later.

faq.q: How do I keep small bags from slipping in?
faq.a: Choose a basket with a bag holder, like the UUJOLY, or fold the bag edge over the rim. Match the bag size to the basket. A loose bag slides down quickly. If your baskets lack a holder, a small elastic band around the rim keeps the liner snug and costs almost nothing.

Good plastic resists chipping, denting and fading, as the listings claim for the JiatuA and JOYMOOP. They can still crack if dropped. Keep them away from heat. Do not leave them next to a space heater or in a hot car, since thin plastic can warp. Lift full baskets by the rim or handle, not by the bag, to avoid stressing the sides.

faq.q: How do I clean small baskets?
faq.a: Wipe the sides with a damp cloth and rinse the inside when something leaks. Smooth baskets like the BGUP wipe quickly. Let them dry before adding a new bag. A damp basket with a bag inside can develop a musty smell, especially in a bathroom. A weekly wipe keeps open baskets looking fresh.
